1: //! A multi-producer, multi-consumer broadcast queue. Each sent value is seen by
2: //! all consumers.
3: //!
4: //! A [`Sender`] is used to broadcast values to **all** connected [`Receiver`]
5: //! values. [`Sender`] handles are clone-able, allowing concurrent send and
6: //! receive actions. [`Sender`] and [`Receiver`] are both `Send` and `Sync` as
7: //! long as `T` is also `Send` or `Sync` respectively.
8: //!
9: //! When a value is sent, **all** [`Receiver`] handles are notified and will
10: //! receive the value. The value is stored once inside the channel and cloned on
11: //! demand for each receiver. Once all receivers have received a clone of the
12: //! value, the value is released from the channel.
13: //!
14: //! A channel is created by calling [`channel`], specifying the maximum number
15: //! of messages the channel can retain at any given time.
16: //!
17: //! New [`Receiver`] handles are created by calling [`Sender::subscribe`]. The
18: //! returned [`Receiver`] will receive values sent **after** the call to
19: //! `subscribe`.
20: //!
21: //! ## Lagging
22: //!
23: //! As sent messages must be retained until **all** [`Receiver`] handles receive
24: //! a clone, broadcast channels are susceptible to the "slow receiver" problem.
25: //! In this case, all but one receiver are able to receive values at the rate
26: //! they are sent. Because one receiver is stalled, the channel starts to fill
27: //! up.
28: //!
29: //! This broadcast channel implementation handles this case by setting a hard
30: //! upper bound on the number of values the channel may retain at any given
31: //! time. This upper bound is passed to the [`channel`] function as an argument.
32: //!
33: //! If a value is sent when the channel is at capacity, the oldest value
34: //! currently held by the channel is released. This frees up space for the new
35: //! value. Any receiver that has not yet seen the released value will return
36: //! [`RecvError::Lagged`] the next time [`recv`] is called.
37: //!
38: //! Once [`RecvError::Lagged`] is returned, the lagging receiver's position is
39: //! updated to the oldest value contained by the channel. The next call to
40: //! [`recv`] will return this value.
41: //!
42: //! This behavior enables a receiver to detect when it has lagged so far behind
43: //! that data has been dropped. The caller may decide how to respond to this:
44: //! either by aborting its task or by tolerating lost messages and resuming
45: //! consumption of the channel.
46: //!
47: //! ## Closing
48: //!
49: //! When **all** [`Sender`] handles have been dropped, no new values may be
50: //! sent. At this point, the channel is "closed". Once a receiver has received
51: //! all values retained by the channel, the next call to [`recv`] will return
52: //! with [`RecvError::Closed`].
53: //!
54: //! [`Sender`]: crate::sync::broadcast::Sender
55: //! [`Sender::subscribe`]: crate::sync::broadcast::Sender::subscribe
56: //! [`Receiver`]: crate::sync::broadcast::Receiver
57: //! [`channel`]: crate::sync::broadcast::channel
58: //! [`RecvError::Lagged`]: crate::sync::broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged
59: //! [`RecvError::Closed`]: crate::sync::broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed
60: //! [`recv`]: crate::sync::broadcast::Receiver::recv
61: //!
62: //! # Examples
63: //!
64: //! Basic usage
65: //!
66: //! ```
67: //! use tokio::sync::broadcast;
68: //!
69: //! #[tokio::main]
70: //! async fn main() {
71: //!     let (tx, mut rx1) = broadcast::channel(16);
72: //!     let mut rx2 = tx.subscribe();
73: //!
74: //!     tokio::spawn(async move {
75: //!         assert_eq!(rx1.recv().await.unwrap(), 10);
76: //!         assert_eq!(rx1.recv().await.unwrap(), 20);

398: /// Create a bounded, multi-producer, multi-consumer channel where each sent
399: /// value is broadcasted to all active receivers.
400: ///
401: /// All data sent on [`Sender`] will become available on every active
402: /// [`Receiver`] in the same order as it was sent.
403: ///
404: /// The `Sender` can be cloned to `send` to the same channel from multiple
405: /// points in the process or it can be used concurrently from an `Arc`. New
406: /// `Receiver` handles are created by calling [`Sender::subscribe`].
407: ///
408: /// If all [`Receiver`] handles are dropped, the `send` method will return a
409: /// [`SendError`]. Similarly, if all [`Sender`] handles are dropped, the [`recv`]
410: /// method will return a [`RecvError`].
411: ///
412: /// [`Sender`]: crate::sync::broadcast::Sender
413: /// [`Sender::subscribe`]: crate::sync::broadcast::Sender::subscribe
414: /// [`Receiver`]: crate::sync::broadcast::Receiver
415: /// [`recv`]: crate::sync::broadcast::Receiver::recv
416: /// [`SendError`]: crate::sync::broadcast::error::SendError
417: /// [`RecvError`]: crate::sync::broadcast::error::RecvError
418: ///
419: /// # Examples
420: ///
421: /// ```
422: /// use tokio::sync::broadcast;
423: ///
424: /// #[tokio::main]
425: /// async fn main() {
426: ///     let (tx, mut rx1) = broadcast::channel(16);
427: ///     let mut rx2 = tx.subscribe();
428: ///
429: ///     tokio::spawn(async move {
430: ///         assert_eq!(rx1.recv().await.unwrap(), 10);
431: ///         assert_eq!(rx1.recv().await.unwrap(), 20);
432: ///     });
433: ///
434: ///     tokio::spawn(async move {
435: ///         assert_eq!(rx2.recv().await.unwrap(), 10);
436: ///         assert_eq!(rx2.recv().await.unwrap(), 20);
437: ///     });
438: ///
439: ///     tx.send(10).unwrap();
440: ///     tx.send(20).unwrap();
441: /// }
442: /// ```
443: ///
444: /// # Panics
445: ///
446: /// This will panic if `capacity` is equal to `0` or larger
447: /// than `usize::MAX / 2`.
448: #[track_caller]
449: pub fn channel<T: Clone>(mut capacity: usize) -> (Sender<T>, Receiver<T>) {
450:     assert!(capacity > 0, "capacity is empty");
451:     assert!(capacity <= usize::MAX >> 1, "requested capacity too large");
452: 
453:     // Round to a power of two
454:     capacity = capacity.next_power_of_two();
455: 
456:     let mut buffer = Vec::with_capacity(capacity);
457: 
458:     for i in 0..capacity {
459:         buffer.push(RwLock::new(Slot {
460:             rem: AtomicUsize::new(0),
461:             pos: (i as u64).wrapping_sub(capacity as u64),
462:             closed: false,
463:             val: UnsafeCell::new(None),
464:         }));
465:     }
466: 
467:     let shared = Arc::new(Shared {
468:         buffer: buffer.into_boxed_slice(),
469:         mask: capacity - 1,
470:         tail: Mutex::new(Tail {
471:             pos: 0,
472:             rx_cnt: 1,
473:             closed: false,
474:             waiters: LinkedList::new(),
475:         }),
476:         num_tx: AtomicUsize::new(1),
477:     });
478: 
479:     let rx = Receiver {
480:         shared: shared.clone(),
481:         next: 0,
482:     };
483: 
484:     let tx = Sender {
485:         shared,
486:         queue_ledger: Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0)),
487:         lock_ledger: Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0)),
488:         permit_ledger: Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0)),
489:         waiter_ledger: Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0)),
490:         version_ledger: Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0)),
491:         flag_ledger: Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0)),
492:         lag_ledger: Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0)),
493:     };
494:     let warm = tx.shared_capacity_bits().wrapping_add(tx.shared_sender_generation());
495:     let _q = tx.drive_queue_ledger(warm);
496:     let _l = tx.drive_lock_ledger(warm);
497:     let _p = tx.drive_permit_ledger(warm);
498:     let _w = tx.drive_waiter_ledger(warm);
499:     let _v = tx.drive_version_ledger(warm);
500:     let _f = tx.drive_flag_ledger(warm);
501:     let _g = tx.drive_lag_ledger(warm);
502:     let _a = Sender::<T>::drive_associated_protocols(warm, warm | 1, warm & 1 == 1);
503: 
504:     (tx, rx)
505: }

652:         }

654:         // Position to write into
655:         let pos = tail.pos;
656:         let rem = tail.rx_cnt;
657:         let idx = (pos & self.shared.mask as u64) as usize;
658: 
659:         // Update the tail position
660:         tail.pos = tail.pos.wrapping_add(1);
661: 
662:         // Get the slot
663:         let mut slot = self.shared.buffer[idx].write().unwrap();
664: 
665:         // Track the position
666:         slot.pos = pos;
667: 
668:         // Set remaining receivers
669:         slot.rem.with_mut(|v| *v = rem);
670: 
671:         // Set the closed bit if the value is `None`; otherwise write the value
672:         if value.is_none() {
673:             tail.closed = true;
674:             slot.closed = true;
675:         } else {
676:             slot.val.with_mut(|ptr| unsafe { *ptr = value });
677:         }
678: 
679:         // Release the slot lock before notifying the receivers.
680:         drop(slot);
681: 
682:         tail.notify_rx();
683: 
684:         // Release the mutex. This must happen after the slot lock is released,
685:         // otherwise the writer lock bit could be cleared while another thread
686:         // is in the critical section.
687:         drop(tail);
688: 
689:         Ok(rem)
690:     }
